summary: Tall BESTÅ cabinet frame with a slide-in back panel, adjustable feet, wall fixing and four shelves, two of them locked in place.
unclear: Exact frame size is not printed; I assumed 600x1920 mm with a 400 mm depth (could be 200 mm).
It is not clear whether the shelf lock supports sit at the back and the pins at the front, or the other way round.
The exact use of the round discs 114931 in step 9 (wall spacer or cover cap) is not clear.
The Ø10 mm drilling in manual step 8 is assumed to be for wall fixing.
Cam lock arrow orientation (roll) was not readable.
The hardware page lists wall fitting 114930 as 1x, but it is one set that splits into two halves (I and II). It is counted here as 2 halves.
The small screws 116637 only fix the shelf lock supports to the side panels (manual step 11). They do not go into a second board; this is what the manual shows.
The back panel width is assumed to fit between the sides in their grooves (564 mm); the real groove depth is not printed.

113301.name: Shelf pin
113301.look: Small L-shaped support with a peg

114667.name: Long screw
114667.look: Long screw with a wide flat head, for joining two frames

114927.name: Cam lock
114927.look: Round metal cam with an arrow and a slot (also numbered 115264)

114928.name: Cam screw
114928.look: Metal pin with a Phillips head and coarse thread

114929.name: Shelf lock support
114929.look: Shelf support with a clip and a screw hole

114930.name: Wall fitting half (I or II)
114930.look: Plastic block marked I or II. Both come joined by pins as one set and are pulled apart.

114931.name: Round plastic disc
114931.look: Flat round disc with a centre hole (also numbered 115982)

114947.name: Adjustable foot
114947.look: Large round foot with a threaded bolt and a hex socket (also numbered 115988)

116637.name: Small screw
116637.look: Short countersunk screw for the shelf lock supports

A.name: Side panel
A.look: Longest boards. One face has rows of small shelf holes and cam-lock holes near both ends. There is a groove near the back edge.

B.name: Top / bottom panel
B.look: Short wide boards with 4 small holes for cam screws and a groove for the back panel. The bottom also has 4 holes for the feet.

C.name: Back panel
C.look: Thin fibreboard sheet as tall as the sides.

D.name: Shelf
D.look: Plain boards with no holes, slightly narrower than the top.

steps.title: Fit cam screws in the top panel
steps.text: Lay one top/bottom panel on a soft surface with the groove facing up. Screw 4 cam screws into the small holes by hand until they sit flush with the collar.
steps.tip: Do not use a power drill. Do not screw them in too deep.

steps.title: Attach the two sides to the top
steps.text: Push both side panels onto the cam screws so their hole rows face inward and their grooves line up with the top's groove. Put 4 cam locks in the holes, arrow toward the pin, and turn them clockwise to lock.
steps.tip: Check that the back grooves of all panels line up before you lock the cams.

steps.title: Slide in the back panel
steps.text: Slide the back panel into the grooves of the sides and the top until it stops. Keep the finished side facing into the cabinet.
steps.tip: Push it all the way in, or the bottom panel will not fit.

steps.title: Fit cam screws in the bottom panel
steps.text: Screw 4 cam screws by hand into the holes on the grooved face of the second top/bottom panel.
steps.tip: Use a screwdriver, not a power drill.

steps.title: Attach the bottom panel
steps.text: Push the bottom panel onto the sides so the back panel slides into its groove. Insert 4 cam locks and turn them clockwise to lock.
steps.tip: Make sure the back panel enters the groove before you push the bottom fully on.

steps.title: Screw in the feet
steps.text: Screw the 4 adjustable feet into the holes on the outside of the bottom panel by hand.

steps.title: Stand up and level the frame
steps.text: Stand the frame upright at its final position. Put a spirit level on top and turn each foot from inside the cabinet with the hex key until the frame is level.
steps.tip: A crooked frame makes doors and shelves fit badly. Level it before you fix it to the wall.
steps.warn: The frame is tall and heavy. Lift it with two people.

steps.title: Split the wall fitting
steps.text: Pull the wall fitting apart into its two halves, marked I and II.

steps.title: Mount the wall fitting halves
steps.text: Turn the frame so you can reach the back. Fit half I at the top on the left side and half II at the top on the right side, pushed up against the top panel. Drill Ø10 mm (3/8") where the fitting shows, using wall fixings that suit your wall.
steps.tip: Do not swap the I and II halves.
steps.warn: Wall screws and plugs are not included. Choose ones that suit your wall material.

steps.title: Fix the frame to the wall
steps.text: Stand the frame against the wall and check that it is level. Fix it to the wall at the top with screws suited to your wall, using the 2 round discs.
steps.tip: Check the level again before you tighten the screws.
steps.warn: The frame must be permanently fixed to the wall to prevent it tipping over. Tip-over can cause serious or fatal crushing injuries.

steps.title: Insert pins for the two middle shelves
steps.text: Push 4 shelf pins into the side holes at the heights you want for the two middle shelves. Use one pin per side for each shelf, with the flat support facing up.
steps.tip: Insert the pins the right way up, as the drawing shows.

steps.title: Fit locking supports and the middle shelves
steps.text: Screw the 4 shelf lock supports into the matching holes with the small screws. Then press the two middle shelves down onto the pins and into the clips.
steps.tip: Fit the supports with the clip facing up. Make sure the supports sit level with the pins.

steps.title: Insert pins for the remaining shelves
steps.text: Push 8 shelf pins into the side holes, 4 for each of the remaining two shelves.
steps.tip: Count the holes so all 4 pins of a shelf are at the same height.

steps.title: Place the remaining shelves
steps.text: Lay the last two shelves down onto their pins.

steps.title: Optional: join two frames
steps.text: If you place two frames side by side, screw them together through the side panel with 3 long screws: top, middle and bottom.
steps.tip: Align the fronts and tops of both frames before you screw.
